'''John Wermer''' was a mathematician specializing in [[complex analysis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.math.brown.edu/faculty/wermer.html |title=Brown University Mathematics Department |website=www.math.brown.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060825084438/http://www.math.brown.edu/faculty/wermer.html |archive-date=2006-08-25}} </ref>

Wermer received his Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]] in 1951 under the supervision of [[George Whitelaw Mackey]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=9742|title=John Wermer}}</ref> He became an instructor at [[Yale University]], after which he was hired as a professor at [[Brown University]] in 1954. He retired in 1994.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mkds.com/obituaries/John-Wermer?obId=25942715#/obituaryInfo |title=Obituary information for John Wermer |website=www.mkds.com}}</ref>

In 1962 Wermer was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Stockholm.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=International Mathematical Union (IMU) |website=www.mathunion.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927014538/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |archive-date=2011-09-27}} </ref>

In 2012, Wermer became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>

On August 29, 2022, Wermer died in [[Providence, Rhode Island|Providence]], [[Rhode Island]] at the age of 95.
<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/obituaries/ppvp0321201 |title=John Wermer |date=6 October 2022 |access-date=2024-02-23 |publisher=[[The Providence Journal]] }}</ref>
